item.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
item.description: In mother-of-pearl suits, the Pearly Kings used to canvass East London for charity. The most famous one, George Major, died in August. A look back on this larger-than-life figure and the Pearly King tradition.

item.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
item.description: Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.

item.title: COMIC: How the census gives your state power (and what Trump wants to change)
item.description: The census is used to determine how much say your state has in Congress and the Electoral College. President Trump failed to alter it during his first term, but he's trying again ahead of 2030.

item.title: Studying this super El Niño could save lives. NOAA is scaling back research
item.description: A powerful El Niño is already influencing extreme weather around the planet. During the last strong El Niño, federal agencies ramped up research in the hope of improving weather forecasts. This year, they won't be matching that effort.

item.title: Egg prices have tumbled since Trump returned to office. Here's why
item.description: Agriculture experts say high egg prices were the result of severe avian flu outbreaks, but the Trump administration's tariffs and the war with Iran have also put pressure on farmers.
